gap_proposals.description: Visible material uses 'rollback works' without specifying the failure mode. The test suite covers failed image verification, the shim describes application-readiness timeout, and the vendor datasheet describes manufacture-time watchdog revert. These can yield opposite conclusions without being the same behaviour.

The manager states that two people give two different accounts of whether rollback works. Independently, test material reports a passing rollback assertion while code material reports no timeout revert compiled in-repo.

One observation is that rollback tests pass on the HITL rig after failed image verification. Another is that timeout revert is not compiled in-repo and the shim retries a new image indefinitely if readiness is never signalled. A third is that 412 field units stopped reporting and did not recover after the spring 2026 update. These claims are incompatible as a general statement that rollback works, and the material contains no authority choosing a winner.
Multiple conflicting observations about rollback exist (human disagreement, passing tests, code path without timeout revert, field non-recovery) and no visible authority resolves them.
The desired understanding that rollback 'actually works' has no measurable success condition (for example which failure modes, time-to-revert, telemetry, or acceptable unreachable-unit count).

There is no explicit method to prove field rollback under the stated constraints. HITL covers image-verification failure only; field units produced no post-update telemetry; recovery observed was physical reflash, not OTA revert.
The vendor datasheet says watchdog-driven revert is configurable at manufacture time, and the material does not record which configuration was applied to units now in the field.
Rollback on device depends on a binary-licensed third-party bootloader whose field configuration and actual revert behaviour are unresolved.

Passing HITL tests for failed image verification are not sufficient to conclude field rollback works. The field failure produced no telemetry, code shows a different no-readiness path without compiled revert, and bootloader field config is unknown.

A prior cellular update left hundreds of units unreachable with no self-recovery and only physical reflash as the observed recovery path. Whether that can recur on the next firmware line is visible and uncontrolled.

It is unclear which units, firmware line, bootloader revisions, stock generations, and failure modes (verification failure, application never ready, watchdog, cellular loss) are in scope for the rollback determination.
Treating in-repo build flags (ROLLBACK_ON_TIMEOUT unset) as the field image configuration lacks supporting evidence; production builds or stock variants could differ.
Affected units were a mix of old and new stock, but there is no record of which recovered units were which, so stock-correlated bootloader or firmware differences cannot be checked.

EV-1 reports roughly 400 unreachable of about 18,000 field units. EV-4 reports 17,600 updated and 412 that stopped reporting. It is unclear whether 17,600 includes the 412, excludes them, or whether the manager figure is a rounding of the same campaign.

No telemetry was received from affected units after the update began, and the material does not identify whether those units failed image verification, never signalled readiness, watchdog-rebooted, lost cellular, or otherwise, so the field incident cannot be mapped to a rollback path.

semantic_proposals.mission: Before shipping the next firmware line, determine whether firmware rollback actually works on fielded soil-moisture sensor units.

semantic_proposals.statement: Establish whether rollback recovers devices after a failed or incomplete over-the-air firmware update.
Avoid another campaign in which unreachable units must be recovered by sending people to farms.
The next firmware line is shipped only after there is a shared, evidence-based understanding of whether rollback will prevent units from remaining unreachable.
Changing the cellular provider contract is out of scope.
Adding a second radio is out of scope.
Rollback behaviour must be understood before the next firmware line is shipped.
Firmware updates must continue to be delivered over cellular from the existing update service, without a second radio and without changing the cellular provider contract.
The bootloader is a third-party component supplied under a binary licence, so field revert behaviour cannot be taken as inspectable source in-repo.
The manager states that about 18,000 soil-moisture sensor units are in the field across 600 farms.
The manager states that last spring an update left roughly 400 units unreachable and required on-farm recovery.
The rollback test suite asserts that after a failed image verification the device boots the previous image, and that suite passes on the hardware-in-the-loop rig.

The bootloader shim marks an image as good once the application signals readiness; if readiness is never signalled, the shim retries the new image indefinitely rather than reverting to the previous slot.
The revert path is compiled only when ROLLBACK_ON_TIMEOUT is set, and no build configuration in the repository sets that flag.
The spring 2026 campaign report records 17,600 units updated, 412 units that stopped reporting and did not recover, and no telemetry from any affected unit after the update began.
Vendor datasheet revision C describes a watchdog-driven revert that is configurable at manufacture time, and nothing in the material records which configuration was applied to units now in the field.

A field service technician states that all 412 affected units were recovered by physically reflashing them, that the units were a mix of old and new stock, and that there is no record of which units were which.
The manager states that two people internally give two different accounts of whether rollback works.
Fielded firmware was built from repository configurations in which ROLLBACK_ON_TIMEOUT is unset.
A passing hardware-in-the-loop test of rollback after failed image verification is treated by some parties as evidence that rollback works in the field.

semantic_proposals.prompt: Does rollback actually work on the units now in the field, and under which failure modes?
Which manufacture-time bootloader revert configuration was applied to units currently in the field, including old versus new stock?

semantic_proposals.question: What manufacture-time bootloader configuration (including watchdog-driven revert) is present on field units?
Did any production or field image, including builds not represented in the repository configurations, compile with ROLLBACK_ON_TIMEOUT set?
